title: 1-byte write before the start of an object
object: a, 24 bytes, allocated after another 24-byte object `first`
neighbour: under a 16-byte-aligned arena *(a-1) is first's last slack byte (first's offset 31)
control: writes a[0], the first valid byte

asan.why: ASan's left redzone on malloc; in an arena the byte is first's alignment slack, poisoned when the allocator unpoisons exactly n.

valgrind.why: As above, via the mempool request's size.

hwasan.why: The preceding granule belongs to another allocation and carries another tag. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: Asymmetry worth reporting: an object's base is aligned to its LowFat region, so an underflow is always out of bounds while an overflow inside the size class is not. LowFat detects case 5 and misses case 1.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc, arena and freelist; server run pending (A5)
